title: Secret White House bunker undercuts Trump’s ballroom lawsuit, ex-officials say
description: The White House already has a nuclear-proof facility buried deep underground and built in secret after 9/11.

title: See photos from the first IndyCar race in Washington
description: Drivers are dashing around the National Mall at speeds expected to exceed 185 mph.

title: Trump’s visa ban on 75 countries struck down by federal judge
description: A federal judge said the indefinite pause, which affected nationals of countries in every corner of the globe, ran afoul of antidiscrimination protections.

title: Pence says U.S.-Canada trade fight adds to affordability concerns for economy
description: “I think the last thing we need right now, as our economy is getting back on its feet, is a trade war with Canada,” the former vice president told CNN.

title: El-Sayed’s win triggered wave of anti-Muslim rhetoric online, Post analysis shows
description: After Abdul El-Sayed won the Democratic Senate nomination in Michigan, conservative commentary about him shifted focus from socialism to his Muslim identity.

title: Becerra, running for governor of California, faces a health insurance problem
description: The nation's uninsured rate hit a historical low when Xavier Becerra was health secretary. Now he wants to be California's next governor as Trump's actions have driven people off health insurance.

title: Trump nominates Cameron Hamilton to lead FEMA (again)
description: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe asks "Politico's" Thomas Frank about new FEMA administrator Cameron Hamilton and whether his appointment means a change in heart by the Trump administration about the agency.

title: Week in politics: primaries results, Iran pressure, Korean relations flip
description: Democrats have not shown a clear preference for progressive candidates over moderate ones. Republicans have rejected some of President Trump's endorsees despite his tight grip on the party's base.

title: The complexities of covering swing voters and what they teach us about politics
description: For Reporter's Notebook, an NPR political correspondent shares the lessons she has learned listening in on groups of swing voters in swing states.

title: She’s a Trump acolyte. He’s a ‘gringo Sandinista.’ Meet the Harps.
description: Trump aide Natalie Harp is estranged from her brother, Preston, who has used social media and recent interviews to criticize her and highlight his own left-wing politics.

title: Week in Politics: Canada talks collapse; U.S. 'Economic D-Day; record national debt
description: Trade talks with Canada collapse hours before a new tariff deadline. President Trump threatens Iran with an "Economic D-Day" the same week the U.S. national debt surpassed $40 trillion.

title: As Canada readies retaliatory tariffs, Mark Carney says his nation is 'at war' with U.S.
description: The U.S. has now imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products. Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada will match those tariffs "dollar for dollar" starting Sept. 8.

title: Supreme Court allows Trump's ballroom construction to continue for now
description: The ruling comes after months of back-and-forth between the Trump administration and the National Trust for Historic Preservation.

title: Top Iran official says U.S. focus on economic warfare shows it has failed militarily
description: The Iranian regime has dismissed President Trump's threats to crush Iran economically, saying that years of U.S. sanctions have failed.

title: What to know about this weekend's IndyCar race on the National Mall
description: Why is the car race in this part of D.C.? Will it be streaming? Who's paying for it? Here's what to know before the Freedom 250 Grand Prix hits the National Mall this weekend.

title: Federal agents seize devices from ex-Rep. Eric Swalwell in sexual misconduct probe, AP source says
description: Federal agents seized electronic devices from former Rep. Eric Swalwell and searched his Washington home as part of an investigation into allegations of sexual misconduct by the ex-Democratic congressman from California.
